messages.recipient_title: Head of Mobile Test Units, SLB Capturi
messages.subject: For Hanne Rolén | SLB Norway / Capturi | Strategic Value Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Rolén,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My mandate spans government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive coordination in a major industrial environment.

SLB's position in Norway, together with SLB Capturi's focus on industrial decarbonisation, is especially relevant to my background. I support stakeholder governance around large renewable-energy investments, coordinate external institutional relationships across multiple regulators and ministries, and recently led a carbon-data proof of concept built from physical operating records to strengthen ownership and traceability.

I prepared a short SLB Norway / SLB Capturi Strategic Value Creation Proposal rather than sending a conventional CV alone. It focuses on public-private stakeholder strategy, carbon evidence, country readiness and executive issue management. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

My strongest fit would be a Director, Head, Country, External Affairs, Sustainability, Strategic Partnerships or energy-transition leadership mandate. I am open to relocation to Norway and employer-supported work authorization.

If this sits outside your current remit, I would be grateful if you would route the proposal to Ole Christian Meldahl, Guillaume Verhaeghe or the appropriate senior leader. I would value a short confidential conversation about where this profile could create value.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Energy Transition, External Stakeholders and Industrial Decarbonisation
strategic_brief.prepared_for_title: Head of Mobile Test Units, SLB Capturi
strategic_brief.executive_summary: SLB's Norwegian platform sits at a valuable intersection of conventional energy, digital technology, subsea systems and industrial decarbonisation. My background is relevant because I operate where technical investment meets public institutions, stakeholder expectations, sustainability evidence and executive decision-making. I lead government and regulatory relations, ESG, social performance, corporate affairs and cross-functional coordination for a multinational mining operation, while supporting renewable-energy deployment and carbon-data governance. I would bring a practical country-facing leadership capability to SLB or SLB Capturi, helping translate market and institutional complexity into stronger stakeholder strategy, project readiness, public-private engagement and accountable execution across energy-transition initiatives.
strategic_brief.company_context: SLB maintains a substantial Scandinavian presence and continues to invest in Norway through oilfield technology, digital solutions, subsea systems and lower-carbon businesses. SLB Capturi is headquartered in Norway and is scaling carbon-capture technology for hard-to-abate industries, where project success depends not only on engineering but also on policy, public-private collaboration, stakeholder confidence, industrial customers and credible sustainability outcomes. The Norwegian business also works closely with major operators on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. This creates a recurring need for leaders who can connect technology and commercial teams with external institutions, stakeholder expectations, local value creation and evidence-based sustainability governance across complex projects and markets.

opportunities.title: Public-private stakeholder strategy
opportunities.rationale: Industrial decarbonisation projects depend on coordinated action among customers, regulators, governments, infrastructure providers and communities. Commercial and technical progress can stall when stakeholder dependencies are not mapped and managed as rigorously as engineering milestones.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build stakeholder architectures that connect institutional relationships, public-policy requirements and customer priorities to project decisions, accountable owners and executive escalation paths.

opportunities.title: Carbon evidence and credibility
opportunities.rationale: Carbon-capture and energy-transition propositions require strong evidence because customers, governments and investors are increasingly sensitive to the quality of emissions baselines, assumptions, ownership and claimed outcomes.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would bring an operating-data mindset to sustainability governance, drawing on a carbon-data pilot built from fuel, electricity, explosives, material movement, production and refinery records with clear source ownership and traceability.

opportunities.title: Country readiness for international growth
opportunities.rationale: Technology businesses expanding into new markets often have strong engineering and commercial capability but still face country-level friction around institutions, permitting, local expectations, partnerships and reputation. These issues can delay otherwise viable opportunities.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support country-readiness assessments, institutional engagement and local stakeholder strategy so market-entry and project teams understand external dependencies early and manage them as part of execution planning.

opportunities.title: Executive issue management
opportunities.rationale: Complex energy projects generate cross-functional issues spanning commercial, legal, sustainability, communications, operations and public affairs. Delay often comes from unclear ownership or weak escalation rather than lack of expertise.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would introduce a practical issue-management rhythm with clear owners, milestones, evidence, decision gates and executive reporting for material external and sustainability matters.

days_0_30: Map priority external stakeholders, project dependencies and country-facing issues across the selected Norway or Capturi scope.
Review how sustainability and stakeholder evidence enters commercial and executive decisions.
days_31_60: Introduce an executive stakeholder and issue register with owners and escalation thresholds.
Build engagement plans around selected customers, authorities and public-private partners.
days_61_90: Advance two priority stakeholder or country-readiness workstreams to measurable outcomes.
Deliver a dashboard connecting external dependencies to project, commercial and sustainability milestones.
days_91_180: Embed the governance model across selected project or market teams.
Use live opportunities to refine country-readiness, stakeholder and evidence standards.

potential_impact: Stronger institutional and public-private alignment around decarbonisation projects.
Better evidence discipline behind carbon and sustainability claims.
Earlier visibility of country and stakeholder risks affecting project execution.
Faster cross-functional resolution of material external issues.
background_relevance: Director-level responsibility spanning government and regulatory relations, ESG, social responsibility, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive coordination within a multinational mining operation.

Senior engagement across institutions responsible for mining, environment, energy, labour, aviation, standards, taxation, trade and investment, with documented follow-through across operating functions.

Stakeholder-governance exposure around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage, plus a carbon-data pilot built from a 52.6 million-litre fuel baseline, 34 entities, 408 monthly entries and 592 equipment IDs.
Experience aligning Environment, HSE, Legal, Finance, Operations, Procurement, HR, Security, Aviation and technical teams around external commitments, evidence and executive decisions.
